restoration_note: Three plagues / three wars by which the self's claim is undone, all proceeding from the light's pressure on darkness. Gaps 0–8 and 10–12 are tightly constrained by editor proposals confirmed through parallel formulas: ⲙⲁⲣϩ̄/bind, ⲁⲧⲙ̄ⲣⲣⲉ/into-the-bond, the qualitative ⲱⲟⲟⲡ, the feminine ordinal Tⲙⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ, the male/female pairing ⲁⲧⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ … ⲧⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ ⲍⲱⲱⲥ, the verb ⲁⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ governed by ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲡⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ, the standard doxological formula ⲱⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲱⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄, the noun ⲡⲏⲩⲉ completing ⲟⲩⲙⲡⲏⲩⲉ "a heaven," and the ⲁⲩⲡⲍ verb confirmed by its cognate object ⲙⲁⲡϩ. Gap 9 (12 chars, no apparatus) is reconstructed from the reading's image of the immovable firmness set between the bolos (where the male self is bound) and the tomb (where the female is enclosed): ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲃⲧ ⲛⲛⲁⲟ̄ "to a great wall," governed by ⲡⲧⲁⲱϩ ⲁ- and qualified by ⲛⲱⲛⲉ "of stone." Confidence moderate on 9, high on the rest.

coptic_restorations.basis: Editor's restoration confirmed: [ⲙⲁ]ⲣϩ̄ completes ⲙⲁⲣϩ̄ (Lyc. of ⲙⲟⲩⲣ 'bind'), continuing ⲁⲩ- from preceding line — 'they bound him in the Living Principle.' Spiritually: the self is bound by the very life it tried to operate as its own.
Editor's restoration confirmed: ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ [ⲁⲧ]ⲙ̄ⲣⲣⲉ = 'inward to the bond' — preposition ⲁ + feminine article ⲧ + extant ⲙⲣⲣⲉ. The interior goods are gathered back into the bond they originally occupied.
Editor's restoration confirmed: [ⲟ]ⲡ completes ⲛⲉϩⲱⲟⲟⲡ, the imperfect-qualitative of ϣⲱⲡⲉ — 'they were existing.' Pure morphological completion.
Editor's restoration confirmed: [Ⲧⲙ̄]ⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ = ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ 'the third (fem.),' agreeing with ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ. Standard enlarged initial Tⲙ̄ marking new section parallel to Tⲱⲁⲣⲡ and Tⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛ̄ⲧⲉ above.
Editor's restoration confirmed: [ⲛⲧ]ⲍⲁⲏ = ⲛ̄-ⲧ-ⲍⲁⲏ 'of the last (era).' Refers to the consummation/last age in which the final separation occurs.
Editor's restoration confirmed: [ⲁⲧⲥ]ⲍⲓⲙⲉ = ⲁ-ⲧ-ⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ 'from the female' — ⲡⲱⲣⲭ governs ⲁⲡⲍⲁⲩⲧ ⲁⲧⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ 'separate the male from the female,' the active vs. receptive forms of self-love.
Editor's restoration confirmed: completes ⲧⲥⲍⲓ-[ⲙⲉ ⲍ]ⲱⲱⲥ 'the female, herself' across the line break, paralleling ⲧⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ in line 19.
Editor's restoration confirmed: ⲛ[ⲁⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ] = future ⲛⲁ-ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'shall be cast,' followed by ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲡⲧⲁⲫⲟⲥ 'inward to the tomb.' The receptive self enclosed in its tomb.
Editor's restoration confirmed: ⲁ[ⲍ]ⲟⲩⲛ = Lyc. ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'inward.' Pure orthographic completion.

Open lacuna of ~12 chars. ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲡⲧⲁⲱϩ ⲅⲁⲣ … ⲛ̄ⲱⲛⲉ governs a noun phrase qualified by 'of stone.' Reading describes the immovable firmness fixed between bolos and tomb forever — Manichaean image of ⲡⲥⲁⲃⲧ ⲛ̄ⲱⲛⲉ 'wall of stone' as the permanent boundary. ⲁ + article ⲡ + ⲥⲁⲃⲧ + adjectival ⲛⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'great' fits the slot: 'they shall reach to a great wall of stone.'
Editor's restoration confirmed: standard Manichaean doxological formula ⲱⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲱⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ 'unto generation of generation, forever and ever,' completing the gap before ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄.
Coptic ⲟⲩⲙⲡ̄[ⲏⲩⲉ] = 'a heaven' (Lyc. ⲡⲏⲩⲉ). The relative ⲡⲉ ⲉⲥⲍⲁⲥⲉ ⲉⲥⲛⲁϣⲧ 'which is bitter and hard' qualifies it. The self's fruit consummated as its own dark heaven.

Editor's restoration confirmed: parallel to ⲁⲩⲡⲍ … ⲁⲩⲡⲁⲣⲭϥ̄ in the next line; cognate-object construction ⲁⲩⲡⲍ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲡϩ 'they have split him with splittings.' Lyc. ⲡⲍ for ⲡⲱϩ. Final separation of the self.

english_restorations.basis: Coptic ⲁⲧ supplies preposition ⲁ 'to' + feminine article ⲧ before extant ⲙⲣⲣⲉ 'bond.'
Coptic Tⲙ̄ supplies the feminine article opening the section heading ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲙⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ 'The Third Plague.'
Coptic ⲛⲧ supplies preposition ⲛ̄ 'of' + article ⲧ before extant ⲍⲁⲏ 'last (era).'
Coptic ⲁⲧⲥ supplies preposition ⲁ + article ⲧ + status-construct of ⲥⲍⲓⲙⲉ 'female': 'separate the male from the female.'
Coptic ⲙⲉ ⲍ completes ⲧⲥⲍⲓ-ⲙⲉ ⲍⲱⲱⲥ 'the female, herself' across the line break from previous segment ending 'the fe-.' ⲍⲱⲱⲥ = reflexive 'herself / also.'

Coptic ⲁⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ (ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ) = 'cast, throw'; future passive 'shall be cast' inward to the tomb. (Coptic ⲍ in gap {8} is morphological completion of ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ already covered by 'inward,' so no separate English placeholder.)

Coptic ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲃⲧ ⲛⲛⲁⲟ̄ governed by ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲡⲧⲁⲱϩ ⲁ- 'they shall reach to,' qualified by extant ⲛ̄ⲱⲛⲉ 'of stone.' Spiritually the immovable firmness fixed between bolos and tomb — the wall of permanent separation.
Standard doxological formula ⲱⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲁ ⲅⲉⲛⲉⲁ ⲱⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ 'unto generation of generation, forever and ever' — closing the second-plague section.
Coptic ⲏⲩⲉ completes ⲟⲩⲙⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'a heaven' begun at the end of the previous line; the self's fruit becomes its own dark, bitter heaven from which there is no further dissolution.
Coptic ⲁⲩⲡⲍ (Lyc. of ⲡⲱϩ 'split, divide') in cognate-object construction with ⲙⲙⲁⲡϩ, parallel to ⲁⲩⲡⲍ ⲛⲡⲁⲣⲭϩ ⲁⲩⲡⲁⲣⲭϥ̄ in the next line — the final triple verb of separation.
